_baseline_provenance: MEASURED 2026-09-13 on the author's Windows box, Node v24.19.0, worktree .claude/worktrees/p3c-skip at master 3c42ab0. Declared value 11. Exact command: `node --test test/tool-preamble-strip-equivalence.test.js` -> `tests 11 / pass 11 / fail 0 / cancelled 0 / skipped 0 / todo 0`, IDENTICAL over six consecutive runs. This spec names ONE test file, so the harness's combined invocation and a per-file invocation are the same argv by construction and there is no per-file-vs-combined gap to report. The harness's OWN counting route (scripts/mutation-harness-utils.mjs) was NOT re-measured locally: it throws at import on Windows ('mutation harness requires git at a trusted absolute path'), so the Linux CI dispatch is the authority for the harness-side number. WHY THIS FILE: it is the file whose observable surface this change edits, and it is the only place the bounded-walk property (drop signal, cap provenance, byte-identity against an unbounded ladder) is pinned. The four mutations that live in src/handlers/chat.js and the eight in src/handlers/tool-emulation.js are each one way the optimization can be silently disabled; because the byte bound is deliberately UNOBSERVABLE in the response, most are killed by the structural test ('the cost bound is still wired from the caller's caps') rather than by a behavioural one. All 12 were verified CAUGHT=12 SURVIVED=0 locally before this spec was added (tmp/perf/p3c-teeth.mjs, same argv, Windows). IF THE BASELINE MOVES: a count change here almost certainly means someone added or removed a test in THIS file, not drift, because the suite has no timers, no child processes and no post-import env reads. Re-measure with `node scripts/spec-baseline-audit.mjs preamble-skip-discarded-tier` and change the number in its own commit; do NOT narrow a mutation to make the spec start.

mutations.name: the byte bound is never installed — the whole point of the change, and nothing stops at the cap again
mutations.anchor: text = t.build(tools || [], toolChoice, callerEnv, modelKey, provider, route, { ...tierOpts, ...t.opts });
mutations.replacement: text = t.build(tools || [], toolChoice, callerEnv, modelKey, provider, route, { ...tierOpts });

mutations.name: the walk stops early but the caller is handed the truncated PREFIX — the ladder then ships it as a tier it must reject
mutations.anchor: if (budget.stoppedByCap && opts.abortAtBytes !== undefined) throw new SchemaCompactTierDropped();

mutations.name: the drop signal is renamed, so the ladder's name check misses it and the prefix escapes as a thrown error
mutations.anchor: constructor() { super("schema-compact tier is over the caller's byte cap"); this.name = 'SchemaCompactTierDropped'; }
mutations.replacement: constructor() { super("schema-compact tier is over the caller's byte cap"); this.name = 'NotTheNameYouCheck'; }

mutations.name: the ladder stops listening for the drop signal — a dropped tier is measured as if it were a real one
the drop bound is derived from a hardcoded 24000 instead of the caller's caps
the drop bound uses the LARGER cap, so a tier rejected at either cap is built in full again
the counter never advances — the byte bound is present but can never bind
the per-node floor is raised until it OVER-counts, which would stop a walk whose finished tier still fit the cap
the bound is checked against the wrong side of the cap (>= stops at exactly the cap)
mutations.anchor: if (budget.byteLimit !== undefined && budget.bytes > budget.byteLimit) throw new SchemaInlineOverBudget();
mutations.replacement: if (budget.byteLimit !== undefined && budget.bytes >= budget.byteLimit) throw new SchemaInlineOverBudget();

mutations.name: the byte cap is ignored when undefined, so an unbounded direct caller now aborts
the cap-stop warning arm is dropped — the stall goes back to being visible only to the node budget
the diagnostic stops saying WHY it stopped — an operator cannot tell a byte-cap stop from node exhaustion

? ' (Stopped early: the inlining had already proven more than the preamble byte cap,'
